transcript:
Header: 2026-07-30 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~42 mins | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Ethan (CSM), Elena, Sanjay, Priya

Summary: quick review of last week's benchmark numbers, discussed caching and batching tradeoffs, clarified cost per 1M tokens and tokens/sec/$, agreed next steps for an extended run with prefix caching and a deeper autoscaling discussion.

Topics: cost/unit economics, tokens/sec per GPU, caching savings (prefix / KV caching), batching tradeoffs (latency vs throughput), quantization impact on cost, security questions (KMS, audit logs)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: alright, hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll do the usual	6 to 40 minute check-in, run through the numbers Maya sent yesterday and then action items. Elena, quick intro?
[00:18] Elena: yeah hi, thanks Jordan. we're mostly here to sanity check cost numbers and see if we can get to the 3x cost reduction target we talked about, uh across our rerank and chat pipelines.
[00:32] Jordan: great, yep. Maya you wanna walk through the slide with tokens per second and the cost model?
[00:37] Maya: sure, so last week we ran the 15 minute synthetic & real-traffic mix on the dL1-80 cluster, we saw about 1,200 tokens/sec for the 1B quant model with default batching, that maps to roughly $0.85 per 1M tokens on hosted, and about $0.42 per 1M tokens on dedicated with reserved capacity assumptions. there is some noise 'cause seq distribution matters.
[01:05] Priya: sorry, can you restate that	6 1,200 tokens/sec is for what profile again?
[01:10] Maya: yeah that's 95th pct tail on our simulated mix, seq lengths around 256 on average, occasional 1k seq for context.
[01:18] Sanjay: surprised that dedicated is almost half	6 what's driving that? is it just reserved pricing or are we seeing better batching?
[01:23] Maya: it's both, dedicated gives you contiguous GPU pools so batching is more efficient and KV cache hits are better because the same model shard stays warm. also we assumed 70% utilization for reserved capacity.
[01:36] Jordan: and remember our cost model assumes prefix caching and aggressive batching improvements by default in the dedicated scenario; hosted baseline didn't include prefix caching savings.
[01:45] Elena: can we quantify the prefix caching savings? we saw a slide but numbers were fuzzy.
[01:49] Maya: rough numbers	6 prefix caching saved about 25-35% tokens emitted for the rerank workload because a lot of context repeats across requests; in terms of tokens/sec/$ that's a ~1.4x improvement on effective throughput. but that varies with dedup rate.
[02:10] Priya: hmm okay. what's the tradeoff with latency? if we batch more aggressively to get tokens/sec up, do we blow up p95?
[02:17] Maya: yes, so batching set to size 32 gives best throughput but p95 latency increases from ~180ms to ~420ms in our test, with some missing cases hitting 700ms. you can tune batching window to balance. we typically recommend latency SLO-driven configs	6 e.g., cap batch window to 50ms for UI query paths.
[02:40] Jordan: right, and we also discussed quantizashun	6 i mean quantization	6 profiles. heavier quant yields ~20-30% cost drop but slightly lower quality on some prompts, so it's a quality vs unit-cost tradeoff.
[02:52] Elena: did the quant tests include int8 or the newer q4_K?
[02:56] Maya: q4_k and int8 both	6 q4_k hit about 18% lower tokens/sec due to some kernel overhead but cost per token still better. transcription note: some kernels were slower on the exact hardware in the synthetic run, so we want an A/B on customer's infra.
[03:10] Sanjay: we'll run A/B on our side. i'll also share real traffic traces. i can send those today.
[03:15] (brief muting, crosstalk)
[03:30] Maya: on caching specifics, we did KV cache warmup for 30 minutes prior, and prefix caching was enabled for 80% of sessions in the mix. with that warmup tokens/sec jumped 20% over a cold start.
[03:46] Priya: warmup time is tricky for our bursty traffic	6 how does Redwood handle cold vs warm start spikes?
[03:52] Jordan: good question	6 we have burst capacity + autoscale policies; for dedicated we can enable short-lived burst nodes and pre-warm using synthetic traffic. the tradeoff is cost for the pre-warm.
[04:05] Elena: on the cost model, can you show the per-query cost estimate for our typical rerank call (avg 320 tokens)?
[04:12] Maya: for 320 tokens, hosted baseline is ~0.00027 per call, dedicated w/ caching and q4_k is ~0.00012 per call, again depends on cache hit rate.
[04:24] Priya: those per-call numbers look good	6 can we get a spreadsheet that ties this to our projected monthly volume?
[04:29] Jordan: yes Jordan: will send updated spreadsheet. (laugh) sorry, i'll send that after the call.
[04:35] Elena: security quick Q	6 KMS integration and audit logs, are those available in the private/dedicated offering?
[04:41] Ethan: yes, we provide KMS/HSM integration and detailed audit logs for Private and Dedicated; we'll include SOC2 docs and network diagrams.
[04:50] Sanjay: network diagrams are important	6 also need to see egress patterns for our VPC.
[04:55] Ethan: noted, i'll include that.
[05:00] Maya: back to the benchmark, one area of confusion I want to flag	6 the tokens/sec/$ metric could be misleading if you include model loading amortization. for short-lived jobs the per-token cost looks worse because load time dominates. we recommended measuring long-running steady-state plus a separate cold-start cost.
[05:18] Elena: our majority traffic is steady but we do have daily batch jobs that spin up workers	6 so we need both numbers.
[05:25] Maya: okay we'll add both.
[05:28] Priya: another operational question	6 what about model fallbacks? if the dedicated cluster is saturated, can requests fall back to hosted variants transparently?
[05:36] Jordan: yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants in hosted region, but you need policies configured for that and a plan for data residency. fallback adds latency and potentially different model quality.
[05:48] Sanjay: fallback is fine as long as it's deterministic and logged.
[05:51] Ethan: we can include trace ids in the call so you can map fallbacks in your logs.
[05:58] (short pause)
[06:10] Maya: quick clarification on numbers	6 the 0.42 per 1M tokens in dedicated assumed 70% utilization and a 12-month reserved commit. if utilization is lower or commit shorter, costs go up.
[06:25] Elena: what's the sensitivity	6 say 50% utilization?
[06:28] Maya: that bumps per-1M cost to ~0.60. so utilization matters a lot.
[06:33] Priya: ok we need to check our forecast of utilization before committing.
[06:38] Jordan: Sanjay said he'd share traces	6 that will help estimate utilization.
[06:42] Sanjay: yes i'll share by EOD.
[06:45] Maya: also small thing	6 batching window tuning per route. for chat endpoints we keep low window, for background scoring we can set bigger windows and use GPU pooling to raise tokens/sec/$ without hurting UX.
[06:58] Elena: do you have a recommended default per-route config?
[07:02] Maya: recommended	6 UI chat: max batch window 50ms, batch size cap 8; background scoring: max batch window 250ms, size cap 64; rerank pipeline: pipelined batching with prefix caching and KV hits prioritized. these are starting points.
[07:20] Priya: good. could you add those to the spreadsheet?
[07:24] Jordan: yes we'll include recommended route configs.
[07:28] Maya: one more experiment idea	6 enable per-client KV cache scoping so that customers with heavy repeated context get better cache locality; there is operational complexity but can improve savings for multi-tenant workloads.
[07:44] Sanjay: that would be useful for our top merchants subset. let's discuss infra implications in the deep-dive.
[07:50] (timestamp jump)
[08:30] Jordan: jumping ahead to risks, biggest thing is utilization and traffic shape mismatch	6 if your actual traffic is burstier you'll hit cold starts and increased cost. second is quality regression from aggressive quantization	6 we need evals on your prompt sets.
[08:48] Elena: we'll run our prompt eval set and share results.
[08:52] Maya: perfect. also we noticed one outlier in the benchmark where a kernel fallback on older GPU drivers caused a 30% perf drop; may be a driver mismatch on your infra	6 Sanjay to confirm GPU driver versions.
[09:05] Sanjay: yep i'll check.
[09:08] Priya: timeline	6 if everything looks good after the extended benchmark, what does the pilot-to-dedicated ramp look like?
[09:15] Jordan: usually 4-6 weeks to stand up dedicated cluster and migrate workloads, includes capacity planning, security review, and canary rollout. with pre-approved contracts and faster procurement could be shorter.
[09:28] Elena: we have procurement timelines of ~6 weeks so that's aligned.
[09:32] Jordan: great.
[09:35] (mid-call, some audio glitches)
[10:00] Maya: ok actionables recap	6 Jordan to send cost spreadsheet; Maya to run the 1-hour run with prefix caching and batching variants; Sanjay to send traces and driver versions; Ethan to share SOC2 and network diagrams.
[10:20] Priya: quick question on SLA	6 do dedicated customers get an SLA for latency p99?
[10:27] Ethan: we provide uptime SLAs; we publish latency SLO guidance and can discuss custom latency SLAs for enterprise contracts.
[10:36] Elena: fine as long as it's in contract terms.
[10:40] Jordan: noted.
[10:45] (short pause)
[11:00] Jordan: any final questions?
[11:05] Priya: none from me.
[11:07] Sanjay: all good.
[11:10] Elena: thanks everyone.
[11:12] Jordan: thanks	6 we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and benchmark date, and schedule the infra deep-dive.
[11:20] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-labeling (Jordan said his own name), minor word swaps (quantizashun => quantization), and kernel/driver names sometimes garbled.
